entries.title: I Samuel 15:1
segments: The reception of special favors lays men under special obligations to hearken attentively to the directions of God, and in all things to follow them.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:2
segments: That which Amalek did;
Though God may delay for a time to punish the wicked, yet he does not forget their sins, and unless they repent, he will in due time punish them according to their deserts.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:4
segments: Telaim; supposed to be a place in the southern part of Judah.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:6
segments:
Kenites; supposed to have been descendants of Jethro. 
 
  Ye showed kindness;
Intimate associations with the wicked are dangerous, and we must separate ourselves from their sins, or we shall share in their punishment.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:7
segments:
From Havilah; in the east border of their country. 
 
  To Shur; in the west border.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:8
segments: All the people; all who fell into his hands.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:9
segments: God requires that some men should be put to death; and in sparing them we may as really rebel against him and expose ourselves to his wrath, a sin taking the life of those whom he requires to be preserved.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:11
segments: It repenteth me; he would change his conduct towards Saul on account of his sins, and would reject him from being king.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:12
segments:
To Carmel; a city in the south part of Judah. 
 
  A place; a monument of his victory.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:13
segments: Men often imagine that they have obeyed God and are entitled to his favor, when their obedience has been only external, and has extended only to a part of his commands.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:14
segments: Facts often show the falsehood of men's professions, and that however high they may stand in their own estimation, they are rebels in the sight of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:16
segments: The Lord's messengers must point out and condemn the sins of rulers as well as of people; and let nothing hinder them from declaring with plainness and fidelity the whole revealed will of God.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:21
segments: Wicked men when convicted of sin often try hard to throw the blame of it on others.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:22
segments: No external attention, even to things which God has commanded, can be accepted as a substitute for an obedient heart.  He is a Spirit, and to be accepted, men must obey him in spirit and in truth.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:23
segments: As the sin of witchcraft; in its guilt.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:25
segments: Multitudes are more anxious to stand well with their fellow men than with God, and often look for pardon to them rather than to him.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:27
segments: He laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle; Saul laid hold upon the skirt of Samuel's mantle, as if forcibly to detain him.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:28
segments: To a neighbor; David.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:29
segments:
The Strength; Jehovah, who had given Israel the victory. 
 
  Nor repent; he would not reverse the sentence he had pronounced against Saul.

entries.title: I Samuel 15:32
segments:
Delicately; or, with pleasure. 
 
  Bitterness--is past; he thought that as Saul had spared his life, he should not now be slain. 
 
When wicked menmost confidently imagine that they have escaped all danger, they may be the nearest to ruin.  There is and can be no security except in the friendship and protection of Jehovah.
